title: Book 3 — Thalia, Chapter 441
paragraphs: It was this Polycrates, then, prosperous in all things, against whom the Lacedemonians were making their expedition, having been invited by those Samians who afterwards settled at Kydonia in Crete to come to their aid. Now Polycrates had sent an envoy to Cambyses son of Cyrus without the Samians' knowledge, while Cambyses was assembling an army to march against Egypt, and had asked him to send to him in Samos and request an armed force. Cambyses, hearing this, very readily sent to Samos asking Polycrates to send a naval force with him against Egypt; and Polycrates picked out those of the citizens whom he most suspected of wanting to rise against him and sent them away in forty triremes, charging Cambyses not to send them back.
